augr.name: augr
augr.description: Go trading system with agents for analysis, debate, and execution.
augr.longDescription: augr runs a multi-agent trading workflow in Go. LLM agents analyze market data, debate their findings, and pass decisions to an execution pipeline.
augr.whyItExists: augr gives market analysis, conflicting views, and trade execution a defined workflow.

clpr.name: clpr
clpr.description: A place to find, organize, and share Twitch clips.
clpr.longDescription: clpr helps people discover Twitch clips, save them into organized collections, and share favorites with other viewers.
clpr.whyItExists: Twitch makes individual clips easy to create but hard to browse and organize later. clpr puts curation first.

clustr.name: clustr
clustr.description: Maps Reddit communities and user interactions as network graphs.
clustr.longDescription: clustr is a network-graph prototype for tracing relationships among Reddit communities and the people who participate in them.
clustr.whyItExists: Reddit splits posts, users, and communities across separate views. A graph makes the links among them inspectable.

cutroom.name: Cutroom
cutroom.description: A staged video production workflow for specialized AI agents.
cutroom.longDescription: The Cutroom prototype assigns specialized agents to defined production stages and records handoffs and attribution as work moves between them.
cutroom.whyItExists: Splitting video work among agents creates an accounting problem. Cutroom records each handoff and contribution in the pipeline.

discord-spywatcher.name: Discord Spywatcher
discord-spywatcher.description: A Discord presence monitor with a web analytics dashboard.
discord-spywatcher.longDescription: The Discord Spywatcher prototype combines a presence-monitoring bot, web dashboard, and REST API for reviewing server activity over time.
discord-spywatcher.whyItExists: Discord shows who is present now. Spywatcher records enough history to inspect longer activity patterns.

echo-trails.name: Echo Trails
echo-trails.description: A map that attaches public stories to real-world locations.
echo-trails.longDescription: The Echo Trails prototype collects public stories and indexes them by the places where they happened.
echo-trails.whyItExists: Indexing stories by location lets people find what others recorded about a place.

edda.name: edda
edda.description: A dungeon master with a Go terminal UI and REST API.
edda.longDescription: edda uses LLMs to run tabletop adventures through a Go terminal interface or REST API. It supports multiple AI providers.
edda.whyItExists: edda gives tabletop sessions a responsive dungeon master that can run through a terminal or API.

galdr.name: galdr
galdr.description: Customer health scores built from Stripe, HubSpot, and Intercom data.
galdr.longDescription: galdr connects Stripe, HubSpot, and Intercom data for B2B SaaS teams. It turns those signals into automated customer health scores.
galdr.whyItExists: Customer risk often appears across several systems before a customer leaves. galdr brings those signals into one score.

internet-id.name: Internet ID
internet-id.description: A creator identity and work-provenance prototype.
internet-id.longDescription: Internet ID focuses on proof of ownership and provenance that leaves original files with their creators and avoids a central verification platform.
internet-id.whyItExists: Creators should be able to prove a work is theirs while retaining the original files.

jury-rigged.name: JuryRigged
jury-rigged.description: A real-time courtroom simulation run by multiple agents.
jury-rigged.longDescription: JuryRigged runs multi-agent courtroom simulations through fixed trial phases. Server-Sent Events carry live updates, and jury agents vote on verdicts and sentences.
jury-rigged.whyItExists: JuryRigged provides a structured setting for testing how agents argue, follow procedure, and reach a group decision.

nearbody.name: nearbody
nearbody.description: Phone-based body doubling for getting difficult tasks started.
nearbody.longDescription: nearbody is a phone-based body-doubling prototype. It pairs someone facing a difficult task with another person who stays on the line while they begin.
nearbody.whyItExists: A phone call makes body doubling available when two people cannot share the same room.

one-block-cinema.name: One Block Cinema
one-block-cinema.description: An iOS coach for making one-to-three-minute films.
one-block-cinema.longDescription: The One Block Cinema prototype guides a filmmaker through planning and making a structured short film on an iPhone.
one-block-cinema.whyItExists: The camera is already in a filmmaker's pocket. One Block Cinema focuses on the process for turning that phone into a finished short.

patchwork.name: Patchwork
patchwork.description: Mutual aid search and coordination built on AT Protocol.
patchwork.longDescription: Patchwork is an AT Protocol mutual aid platform. It includes a web client, query API, ingestion and indexing pipeline, and moderation worker.
patchwork.whyItExists: Patchwork makes mutual aid requests searchable and moderatable while keeping the network on an open protocol.

pocket-civilization.name: Pocket Civilization
pocket-civilization.description: A lifelog simulator that turns personal traces into a small civilization.
pocket-civilization.longDescription: Pocket Civilization uses passive lifelog data to shape a small simulated world that changes over time.
pocket-civilization.whyItExists: Pocket Civilization represents personal history as changes in a simulated world instead of rows on a dashboard.

soundhash.name: soundhash
soundhash.description: Audio fingerprint search for matching sounds across social video clips.
soundhash.longDescription: soundhash stores audio fingerprints in PostgreSQL and searches them for matches across videos from different social platforms.
soundhash.whyItExists: A reused sound can lose its source after a few reposts. Fingerprint matches can reconnect those copies.

subcorp.name: Subcorp
subcorp.description: A self-hosted workspace planned for six AI agents.
subcorp.longDescription: Subcorp is being designed for six agents to share tool execution, automated workflows, roundtable conversations, and semantic memory in one self-hosted workspace.
subcorp.whyItExists: Coordinating six agents means sharing tools, memory, and conversation state. Subcorp keeps those pieces in one self-hosted workspace.

subcult-tv.name: subcult.tv
subcult-tv.description: The Subculture Collective website and project catalog.
subcult-tv.longDescription: subcult.tv is the public website for Subculture Collective. It contains the homepage, project catalog, zine archive, and published updates.
subcult-tv.whyItExists: This site keeps the collective's projects, writing, and updates in one public place.

paqr.name: paqr
paqr.description: Packages research files and metadata into searchable HDF5 datasets.
paqr.longDescription: paqr turns research files, notes, tables, and metadata into documented HDF5 packages. Users can inspect them from the command line, serve them through an API, or browse them in a lightweight interface.
paqr.whyItExists: Research context gets lost when data is spread across unrelated files. paqr keeps the data, metadata, and provenance together for reuse and reproduction.

redstring.name: redstring
redstring.description: A litigation workspace for evidence, filings, and deadlines.
redstring.longDescription: redstring is a developing workspace where paralegals and lawyers can organize documents, filings, deadlines, communications, and facts into a verified case record.
redstring.whyItExists: Every case claim needs a source, even as filings and deadlines change. redstring keeps that chain attached to the rest of the case record.

hasanara.name: hasanara
hasanara.description: Search, link, and export transcripts from YouTube videos and channels.
hasanara.longDescription: hasanara ingests YouTube videos or channels and transcribes them with Whisper, with optional speaker diarization. It stores jobs and transcripts in PostgreSQL and provides search, deep links, and exports through a FastAPI backend and React frontend.
hasanara.whyItExists: Video archives are difficult to search or cite. hasanara turns their speech into text that people can find, link, quote, and export.

vod-tender.name: vod-tender
vod-tender.description: Archives authorized Twitch VODs and their live chat.
vod-tender.longDescription: vod-tender is a Go service that discovers Twitch VODs, downloads authorized archives with yt-dlp, and records live chat with each VOD. A small API and frontend can also manage uploads to YouTube.
vod-tender.whyItExists: Twitch archives expire, and video downloads often omit the chat. vod-tender helps creators preserve both parts of their own broadcasts.

subcults.name: subcults
subcults.description: A discovery network for local and underground music scenes.
subcults.longDescription: The subcults design maps local music scenes through events, posts, live audio sessions, memberships, alliances, and trust relationships, with community control and privacy built into the model.
subcults.whyItExists: Location, participation, and trust say more about a local scene than a popularity ranking. subcults organizes discovery around those relationships.

artemis.name: artemis
artemis.description: A mission-control dashboard prototype for NASA Artemis missions.
artemis.longDescription: artemis brings schedules, mission phases, media, updates, explanations, and available telemetry into a single developing interface.
artemis.whyItExists: Following one Artemis mission can mean checking NASA schedules, news posts, media libraries, and trackers. artemis collects that material in one console.

clustr-galaxy.name: clustr-galaxy
clustr-galaxy.description: A Unity prototype for navigating community graphs in 3D.
clustr-galaxy.longDescription: clustr-galaxy places community data in a navigable Unity scene organized into clusters, constellations, and discovery layers.
clustr-galaxy.whyItExists: Large community graphs crowd a flat screen. clustr-galaxy uses spatial navigation to separate and inspect their clusters.

blacktower.name: blacktower
blacktower.description: Runs parallel OpenCode agent labs from a web control center.
blacktower.longDescription: blacktower provisions OpenCode labs and delegates work to pools of background sessions. Its keyboard-driven web app tracks agents, streams, health checks, schedulers, and sessions.
blacktower.whyItExists: Running several agents at once requires a clear view of their work and health. blacktower provides that control center.

switchyard.name: switchyard
switchyard.description: Schedules automated agent workflows and shows their runs and queues.
switchyard.longDescription: switchyard manages schedules, runs, queues, and pinned agents for automated workflows. Its HUD-style dashboard exposes pipelines, logs, prompts, skills, and operational data.
switchyard.whyItExists: Automated workflows are hard to operate when their decisions and failures stay hidden. switchyard makes each run inspectable.

dsa-seats.name: DSA Seats
dsa-seats.description: Tracks congressional races, district maps, and sourced election data.
dsa-seats.longDescription: DSA Seats tracks congressional races and gathers election datasets by state. It includes correction and verification flows, campaign finance availability checks, and district maps with seat breakdowns.
dsa-seats.whyItExists: Election data comes from many sources and often needs correction. DSA Seats keeps the source and verification work visible while making races easier to browse.

roberts-rules.name: Roberts Rules
roberts-rules.description: A meeting and motion engine built on AT Protocol.
roberts-rules.longDescription: Roberts Rules models deliberative meetings with AT Protocol lexicons. It records meeting state, motions, voting strategies, replay data, and outbox publications for verifiable public procedure.
roberts-rules.whyItExists: Meeting procedure is difficult to verify when only the chair tracks it. Roberts Rules creates a shared record of motions and votes.

productivity-suite.name: Productivity Suite
productivity-suite.description: Local-first task and project planning with CalDAV sync.
productivity-suite.longDescription: Productivity Suite manages tasks, projects, templates, choice pools, and recovery tasks locally. Its CalDAV-aware sync engine connects to Google and Baikal, and an Electron shell provides a desktop app.
productivity-suite.whyItExists: Productivity Suite keeps planning available offline, then syncs it through services the user chooses.

subcult-pds.name: subcult-pds
subcult-pds.description: A self-hosting kit for an AT Protocol personal data server.
subcult-pds.longDescription: subcult-pds packages an AT Protocol personal data server for a one-command launch. It includes Compose services, deployment scripts, documentation, and backup guidance.
subcult-pds.whyItExists: subcult-pds gives communities a repeatable way to host and back up the server that holds their identities.

subcult-os.name: subcult-os
subcult-os.description: Event planning, ticket scanning, and door tools for live scenes.
subcult-os.longDescription: subcult-os includes a web workspace for events, door operations, and run-of-show planning. Its React Native app gives hosts ticket scanning, invite management, and public event pages.
subcult-os.whyItExists: Small live events need practical tools for the door, guest list, schedule, and tickets without piecing together unrelated apps.

invisible-museum.name: Invisible Museum
invisible-museum.description: An iOS prototype for placing virtual exhibits in physical spaces.
invisible-museum.longDescription: Invisible Museum uses SwiftUI and ARKit to overlay virtual exhibits on physical locations. Current work covers AR sessions, HUD projection, exhibit entities, saved collections, and contributions.
invisible-museum.whyItExists: An exhibit tied to a location can wait there for the next visitor. Invisible Museum is working out how people place, save, and contribute to one.

tmux-popups.name: tmux-popups
tmux-popups.description: Opens calculators, notes, file browsers, and scripts in tmux popups.
tmux-popups.longDescription: tmux-popups maps entries in a popups.tsv manifest to quick tmux windows for calculators, notes, file explorers, and scripts.
tmux-popups.whyItExists: Small terminal tasks should not require leaving the current tmux session or rebuilding its layout.

obsidian-plugin-metronome-tuner.name: obsidian-plugin-metronome-tuner
obsidian-plugin-metronome-tuner.description: A metronome and chromatic tuner inside Obsidian.
obsidian-plugin-metronome-tuner.longDescription: obsidian-plugin-metronome-tuner adds a metronome and chromatic tuner to Obsidian. It analyzes microphone input locally on desktop and mobile.
obsidian-plugin-metronome-tuner.whyItExists: Musicians can practice against a tempo or check pitch without switching away from their Obsidian notes.

omarchy-plugin-shelfish.name: omarchy-plugin-shelfish
omarchy-plugin-shelfish.description: Groups Omarchy bar widgets into named, collapsible shelves.
omarchy-plugin-shelfish.longDescription: omarchy-plugin-shelfish organizes Omarchy bar widgets into named groups that users can collapse. It includes translations for ten languages.
omarchy-plugin-shelfish.whyItExists: Collapsible groups keep a crowded desktop bar organized while leaving its widgets close at hand.

omarchy-plugin-superproductivity.name: omarchy-plugin-superproductivity
omarchy-plugin-superproductivity.description: Controls Super Productivity tasks from the Omarchy top bar.
omarchy-plugin-superproductivity.longDescription: omarchy-plugin-superproductivity adds a top-bar widget and panel for the current Super Productivity task. It also shows Today's tasks, supports quick add, and displays alerts.
omarchy-plugin-superproductivity.whyItExists: The plugin keeps the active task and common controls visible without opening the full app.

omarchy-plugin-topbar.name: omarchy-plugin-topbar
omarchy-plugin-topbar.description: Sets a separate Omarchy top-bar layout for each monitor.
omarchy-plugin-topbar.longDescription: omarchy-plugin-topbar gives each monitor an independent Omarchy bar layout. Users can choose full, minimal, or hidden modes and scope workspaces by monitor.
omarchy-plugin-topbar.whyItExists: Different monitors often serve different jobs. The plugin lets each screen use its own bar and workspace setup.
